title: West Woods
summary: West Woods is a forty acre beach and woodland area owned by the Shinnecock Tribe. The woodland and beach area is used for contemporary social gatherings, weddings, celebrations, camping, and sweat lodge ceremonies. In recent times, West Woods has been encroached upon with it's blurred boundaries. At the start of the 1747 100-year timber lease to the Shinnecock by Southampton Town, the land encompassed one hundred acres.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Shinnecock Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: This forty-acre tract of beach and woodland serves as an active, contemporary gathering space where Shinnecock tribal members continue to host community weddings and sweat lodge ceremonies. Defending these vital communal spaces against modern boundary encroachment demonstrates that Native cultural practices are living traditions permanently rooted in the Long Island landscape.
history_content:
1885 During a Shinnecock Tribal Meeting, the tribe voted that the tribe defend any one who might be sued for cutting wood in the west woods. 1 The earliest record of West Woods appears in Belcher Hyde's 1916 map. Again in the later 1929 Dolph Stewart map.

Westwoods public land-rights source

A Dans Papers article on Westwoods described the area through a public land-rights dispute rather than as empty shoreline. It supports the Cassady-related calendar entry by showing Westwoods as part of a continuing Shinnecock sovereignty and land-defense history.

Source: Dans Papers, Sorting Out a 350 Year Old Real Estate Sale, project archive / Shinnecock Archaeology and History Drive folder.
